prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this tunable moire system.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B014 as a sole prize part, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. After the full round-1 exchange the scientific case looks, if anything, clearer to me. The mechanism is simple and analytic (interlayer tunnelling drives the Dirac velocity to zero at a magic angle in the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model), the prediction predates the data by seven years, and the 2018 experiments found strongly correlated insulating and superconducting states in precisely the tunable system the model singled out. Everyone who supports B014 names the same three people and words the citation around prediction plus observation, not around the pairing mechanism, which tells me the credit is as stable as it can be on the supplied packet. The chair's summary also records that the continuum model is now routinely used as the starting point for the moire literature, which is the sign of a foundational idea rather than a fashionable one. The phenomenology has been reproduced by transport, STM and spectroscopy in many groups, and the twist angle and gate voltage act as a new, continuously tunable control knob on correlated matter. That is a new regime, not a refinement, and it has no overlap with a recent prize.
statement.case_against: The credit question remains the real weakness and the discussion did not remove it. Eva Andrei's STM and transport work on flat-band localisation in twisted layers is independent experimental support for the flat-band picture, Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, cannot fit under a three-person cap, and the earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Shallcross) is not covered. Second, the pairing mechanism is unsettled and twist-angle disorder limits quantitative reproducibility, so a cautious committee could wait. Third, if the committee insists on a mature, closed topic, the optical lattice clock (B013) is the stronger candidate on that axis, and I would not call its choice a scientific error, only a different weighting of novelty against maturity.

responses.point: Kroll ranked B014 last because twist-angle disorder limits sample-to-sample reproducibility and the superconducting mechanism is unsettled, so he does not know what a prize would be certifying; he prefers the lattice clock because its uncertainty budgets are published and cross-checked.
responses.response: I accept the measurement standard and I agree that B013 passes it better than B014 does. But the question the prize must answer is what it certifies, and my answer is narrow: that flat bands appear at a magic angle, and that correlated insulating and superconducting phases appear in that system. Both are reproduced qualitatively by many groups, and disorder changes the details of transition temperatures and gap sizes, not the existence of the phases or the location of the magic angle within the known spread. The pairing mechanism is not part of the claim, exactly as the 1986-87 cuprate prize did not wait for a theory of high-temperature superconductivity. I would also note that the clock's strength, maturity, is the very feature that makes it close to 2005 and 2012, which you and Lindroth raise against it yourselves. I would not overrule you on weighting, but I do not think disorder is a bar to a citation worded this way.

responses.point: Lindroth keeps the optical lattice clock first, as a fundamental advance in measurement reproduced across continents, and asks whether the unresolved superconductivity weakens B014 enough to put it behind the clock; she also lists overlap with 2005 and 2012 as an open issue.
responses.response: Your own uncertainty list contains the point I find decisive: you are unsure whether the overlap with the frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes is disqualifying. I would not call it disqualifying, but when I ask what is new in nature, the lattice clock is a better instrument for a measurement already recognised in kind, whereas a gate-tunable flat band is a regime nobody could previously reach. You and the chair also say Ye's credit is shaded by the Hall lineage and that Paris, PTB and JILA all contributed, which makes the two-name cut harder than the three-name cut for B014, where all five supporters converge on the same set. I answer the maturity concern as I did to Kroll: the citation does not rely on the unsettled part. I keep B013 as my first alternative and would be content if the committee preferred it, but I do not think the maturity gap is large enough to reverse my ranking.

responses.point: Olsson would keep Bistritzer beside MacDonald, says dropping him does not resolve the Andrei question because her case rests on experimental evidence, and would want an expert report on priority between Andrei's STM work and the 2018 transport discovery.
responses.response: I agree and I now hold the position more firmly than in round 1. The 2011 prediction is a two-author paper and Bistritzer is not a later bystander, so dropping him to create a seat would trade a clean, traceable theory credit for a contested experimental one. Your point that the Andrei claim is experimental also sharpens my own view: her STM results show flat-band localisation, but the 2018 papers established the correlated insulating and superconducting phases, which is the step the citation actually names. If expert reports show her priority on the flat band itself is decisive, I would prefer to revisit the experimental half, either by replacing Jarillo-Herrero with a different pairing or by restricting the citation, not by taking away Bistritzer. On the present packet I do not see grounds to alter the trio.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B014 first for the theory-experiment loop, treats Andrei as a possible but not necessary displacement, and regards the lattice clock as precision engineering built on the 2005 recognition.
responses.response: We agree on the structure and on the weakness of the clock as a candidate for novelty, and in round 1 I pressed you on how far Andrei's claim goes. After reading the other statements I think we are close to the same conclusion: the chair's summary shows that supporters differ only on whether to build on the trio, not on who is in it. Where I remain more cautious than you is on B041, which you rank second; the 2016 prize covers the topological idea and the allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and the omitted BHZ authors is much less clean. I would therefore place B013 above B041 as an alternative, and I would not support a two-part B014 plus B013, because it would dilute the strongest single case and give the clock a prize slot it does not need in order to be recognised later.

responses.point: Danielsson moved from B016 to B014 after the openings, names maturity of interpretation and the Andrei attribution as the strongest reservations, and keeps B016 and B041 as alternatives.
responses.response: I welcome the move and I think your framing of maturity, interpretation rather than phenomenon, is the correct one: the prize honours a prediction and a discovery, not an understanding of the superconductivity. On your condition about Andrei, I agree that if experts call her contribution decisive rather than supporting, the trio is wrong, and I would say so in my final ballot. I differ on B016 as an alternative: with Halzen alone credited for a collaboration-scale discovery, the allocation is the thinnest on the shortlist, as Pearce himself concedes, and I would not choose it unless outside experts supply a defensible name set.

uncertainties: Whether outside experts will judge Eva Andrei's STM flat-band work to be independent and decisive for the flat-band claim, which would force a change in the experimental half of the credit, and whether Yuan Cao's role changes the cut.
Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder make B014 premature for colleagues who weight maturity most heavily, and what evidence would move them.
Whether the continuum-model precursors (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Shallcross) deserve credit that a three-person cap cannot provide.
Whether B013 would be preferred by the committee on maturity grounds; my fallback ordering of B013 over B041 depends on how the 2005 and 2016 overlaps are weighed.
My recollection of dates and author lists is from memory and should be checked against the primary literature.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. I have no collaboration with or institutional tie to any credited person on B014 or the other shortlisted candidates that I am aware of. I am a Gothenburg theorist and share an institutional environment with Chalmers colleagues; Goran Johansson's declared closeness to B046 does not touch my configuration, which does not include B046. I note Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce's disclosures as relating to B013 and B016, which are only my alternative or outside my configuration.
